function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "is any vpn is installed". They want to check if any VPN is installed. We need to use the cmd_controller_execute tool to run a command that checks for installed VPNs. On Windows, we can query installed programs via PowerShell: Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Where-Object { $_.Name -like "*VPN*" } or use wmic product get name. But wmic product is slow. Alternatively, we can check registry keys under HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall and HKCU. But simplest: use wmic product get Name | findstr /i "vpn". That will list installed products containing "vpn" in name.

We should call cmd_controller_execute with command: "wmic product get Name | findstr /i \"vpn\"". That will output names of installed products containing "vpn". If nothing found, output will be empty. We can then parse output. But the tool returns whatever the command outputs. So we can just return the output. The user might want a yes/no answer. But we can provide the list. Let's do that.
